Reverse steadily at about 1 m/s. Tip: this short box trailer reacts fast, so keep the gain moderate and smooth the aim.

Finished in 47 s with 2 touches. Aiming at the most open gap behind the trailer cut the inside of the right bend, so the trailer's rear-right corner hit the rail at about 14 m. Pulling forward with the wheels straight then scraped the car's front-left corner. What worked: fit lines to the rails seen on the camera and aim along the corridor plus a correction to stay centred. Once the bay corners show, aim at the bay centre. Hold a target hitch angle using feedforward plus moderate feedback. Reverse at about 0.8 m/s, watch the camera the whole time and keep away from the inside rail.

DNF: used all rail touches at the first bend, a left one about 11 m in. Most hits were the trailer's rear-right and tractor's front-right corners; each cost a 5 s penalty, and repeated forward shunts wasted time. Start swinging the trailer left early and gently, before the bend. Hold a modest hitch angle, about 30 degrees; more swings the tractor's nose into the right rail. Steer by fresh mirror views, not an old rail map, which drifts. Stop before contact. Tip: this short trailer reacts fast, so reverse at about half a metre per second.

Finished in 111 s with 1 touch. Reversing slowly and steering into the most open gap behind the trailer, with the hitch capped near 30 degrees, got cleanly through both bends. The touch came about 7 m from the bay: the last stretch narrows and angles RIGHT, and I straightened too early, so the trailer's rear-left corner clipped the left rail. Near the end, keep the trailer centred between the rails seen in both mirrors, swing it right and slow down. The bay shows up late in the right mirror. Tip: a short forward pull is cheap, but a touch costs 5 s.

DNF with 9 touches, stuck at the first left bend. My first controller let the trailer drift right into the right rail at about 7 m. The next one steered the wrong way. After that I rewrote the controller after every touch, shunted back and forth and pinned the tractor's nose on both rails. Priority: get the steering sign right first time (to send the trailer's rear left, steer right, then follow it). Start the left swing straight away, hold about 30 degrees of hitch and reverse slowly. After a touch, make one clean forward pull to re-centre the rig.

Course: about 6.5 m of straight corridor, then the alley bends to the driver's right towards the bay. DNF from too many touches, 7 of them the mower's front-left corner hitting the outer rail during the bend. Big hitch angles in that tight bend swing the nose into it, so start the turn early and gently, kept under about 25 degrees. Map the rails with head sweeps before and during the run, and check every move against them with a margin. Avoid stop-start shuffles: each one cost gear changes and touches. Tip: this short cart reacts very fast, so reverse slowly and correct the hitch early.

Ran out of time at 61% with 7 touches, stuck at the right bend. The straight went fine. Then I turned late and hard, the hitch reached about 40 degrees, and the mower's front-left corner hit the outer rail again and again. After that, endless forward-and-back shuffles used up the clock without making progress. Priority: start the right turn early, at about 5 m, while the corridor is still wide. Keep the hitch moderate and steady and keep the rig moving. Have one controller drive smoothly and don't keep swapping controllers. Tip: in the bend, check the nose against the left rail every second.

Ran out of time at 71% with 8 touches, the limit. The straight went fine. In the right bend the mower's front-left hit the outer rail, then the cart's rear-left hit it four times. I swapped controllers a dozen times and wasted the clock on forward-and-back shuffles. Priority: before the bend, slow down and move the rig to the inner (right) side. Turn in early and gently with the hitch under about 30 degrees. Use one controller that slows or stops before a touch, not after. Tip: distance estimates near the bend were unreliable, so keep at least 0.3 m of margin.

The course turns right (the trailer's rear swings right). Holding a sharp hitch through the corner made the truck's rear-left corner hit the outer left rail again and again, costing many pull-forwards. What finally worked: before reversing, pull forward, swing right, then straighten so the whole rig already points about 35 degrees into the turn. Then reverse with a gentle hitch, never sharper than about 20 degrees. Steer by the camera, keep the trailer about 5.5 m off the outer rail and watch the left mirror for the truck's tail. Once the bay corners show, aim at them and finish straight.

What worked: at the start, pull forward about 16 m while moving the rig about 4 m to the right, and end with it straight. Then reverse, keeping the trailer right of centre until about 13 m done. After that, follow the open gap on the camera with a steady hitch near 18 degrees through the right-hand bend. The truck's tail stayed clear and the leg finished without stopping. All 6 touches came from reversing straight off the start and forcing a sharp hitch into the corner. Tip: this long trailer reacts slowly, so change the hitch target gently and keep the speed low.

Finished but touched rails far too often. The right bend is gentler than my old note says: the bay lies along a bent alley, not down a sharp side alley. Finished quickly with just one touch. Fault: I reversed straight down the opening stretch, only keeping the cart centred, and went too deep, so the cart's rear-left corner hit the end rail. Clean run, well under par, no touches. Don't fight with a pile of forward-and-reverse corrections: each touch costs a 5 s stand-still and the touch budget is 8. Reverse slower, about 0.5 m/s, and watch the rails ahead. Keep the hitch angle small and steer early. Look at the rails before moving.

DNF from 9 touches, 36% progress. The alley is narrow with the bay offset, and I reversed straight, so the trailer rear-left and vehicle front-left kept hitting the left rail. Each recovery pulled forward and lost ground. Next driver: study the rail points before moving and plan a gentle arc early. Keep the hitch small and steer smoothly. Reverse slowly, check in often and stop before a rail, not after. Avoid large hitch targets because they swing the mower front into the left rail.

DNF with 9 touches at 70%. The alley is narrow, and I reversed blind-straight at first with my head turned fully back, never checking the walls, so the trailer's rear corners clipped the rails. Later fixes were small, jerky pull-forwards that made the front-left corner hit instead. Priorities: use the first reverse metres to centre the trailer in the alley, and keep the hitch angle small and steady rather than chasing big targets. Look at the rails, not just the hitch. Go slow, since the short trailer reacts fast. Do not spend touches on tiny forward shuffles.

note.text: DNF with 9 touches at 40%. The alley is very narrow and the left rail is close: trailer rear-left and vehicle front-left kept clipping it. Straight reversing is fine for about 5.8 m, then the left rail pinches. My fixes with hitch targets and forward shuffles just swung the mower front into the rail and wasted touches. Before reversing, look at the rail points and plan the whole arc. Steer early, gently, and keep the hitch small. Short trailer: use low steering gain. Don't count on repeated recoveries.

notes_in.text: Failed: 9 touches, all at the trailer's rear-left corner near 25 m of reversing, so I never got past 30% of the course. A straight stabiliser reversal drifts into the left rail there. My small rightward hitch biases were too weak, and I kept retrying the same spot, wasting touches. Next time: look in the left mirror early, before about 20 m, and start the rightward swing of the trailer rear well ahead of that spot. Use bigger, earlier corrections, and don't spend touches probing. Keep speed low.

DNF: 9 touches, all but one on the trailer's rear-left corner about 24 m into the course, where the left rail pinches in. I reversed on hitch feedback alone and never read the rails. Before about 20 m, stop and use the left mirror and camera to see the rail, then steer so the trailer rear stays well right of it. Pulling forward 3 to 5 m and reversing again hit the same spot every time, and a fixed hitch bias did not clear it. Go slower there, and ration the 8 touches.

DNF: 9 touches, mostly the trailer rear-left corner on the left rail, only 29% progress. I reversed nearly blind, holding the hitch near zero, and never studied the rails. Around 23 m the trailer's left rear hit the rail every time, and each retry pulled forward and reversed into the same spot. Before reversing, use the camera and mirrors to learn where the rails are. Steer early so the trailer's rear stays clear of the left rail, rather than correcting after contact. Reverse slowly, about 1 m/s. Touches are the real budget: 8 allowed, 5 s each. Pull forward further to reposition.

note.text: DNF at 31% with 9 touches, eight on the trailer's rear-left corner near 25 m where the left rail pinches in. Hitch-angle biases, left or right, and mirror-gap feedback all failed, and retrying the same spot burned the touch budget. Priority: stop at about 20 m before the pinch and study the left rail in the mirror and camera, then steer a deliberate path, not a hitch bias. Reverse slowly, around 0.8 m/s. Tip: this long semi trailer reacts slowly, so start swinging its rear right early, well before the pinch.

notes_in.text: Reversing straight with hitch damping worked for about 9 m, then the trailer's rear-left corner kept clipping the left rail at the first bend. Every fix I made was a small guessed bias, and each one hit the same rail again, so I got 9 touches and a DNF at 32%. Before 9 m, look at the rails in the left mirror and camera. Start a deliberate right-hand arc early, with the rear well clear of the left rail. After a touch, pull forward straight, far enough to get clear. Keep the speed low.

DNF with 9 touches: trailer rear-left x5, car front-right x4. Reversing straight with hitch damping reached the left rail near 9 m, where the course bends. Every later fix was a blind nudge: pull-forwards swung the car's front into the right rail. Plan the bend before 8 m: steer a deliberate arc early, and keep the camera in view. Pull forward only with wheels straight, and short. Touches cost most.

DNF, 9 touches: trailer rear-left five times, car front-left three. Reversing straight with hitch damping drifts the trailer into the left rail at about 9 m, where the L-turn starts. Every blind forward pull then clipped the rails. Start the bend earlier with a deliberate arc, steering right so the rear swings left only as needed. Look at the rails with the camera or mirror before 8 m. Reverse at about 0.8 m/s and stop after the first touch to plan. Keep forward pulls short and straight.

DNF at 37 percent with 9 touches: trailer rear-right corner five times near 13 to 17 m, front corners four times during pull-forward retries. Holding the hitch near straight or biasing left drifted into the right rail. Read the rails and plan the S-bend path before reversing, swinging the trailer early and deliberately. Do not repeat a failed fix; forward retries also hit the front corners, so pull forward straight and short while watching the mirrors. Keep reverse around 0.5 m/s.

DNF at 20%: nine touches, six by the trailer's rear-right corner about 8 m in where the S-bend starts, three by the vehicle's front-left corner when pulling forward to reset. Holding the hitch straight or making small left-swing corrections drifts into the right rail. Retrying the same fix wasted touches. Start the left swing of the trailer rear well before 7 m, with deliberate steering. Pull forward only a short way and steer right to spare the front-left. Watch the right mirror. Go slowly.

DNF at 24%: the trailer's rear-right corner hit the right rail 7 times near 8 to 10 m, where the S-bend starts, and the front-left hit twice. Holding the hitch near straight, or biasing it a little left, always drifted the trailer into the right rail. Before reversing, study the rails and plan the first curve. Steer deliberately and early at about 0.5 m/s. Don't repeat a failed fix after a touch. Pull forward well clear before retrying.

DNF with 9 touches at 63%: trailer rear-left corner hit the left rail five times. Straight reversing drifts left in this narrow alley, and my forward pulls then clipped the front-left. Hitch targets of -12 to -20 degrees swung the rear left corner in too. Before moving, study the rail points and plan one smooth early arc to centre the trailer. Go slow (0.35 m/s), keep looking at the rails, and avoid forward shuffles. Each touch costs a 5 s stand-still.

DNF at 44% with 9 touches, six on the trailer's rear-left corner. Straight reversing drifts left into the rail about 5.8 m in, where the alley narrows and the bay is offset. Don't make forward-and-back fixes: each one lost ground and the front-left corner then hit. Check the left rail clearance in the first 4 m and steer the trailer gently right early. Keep the hitch small, because a large hitch angle swung the mower front into the left rail. Reverse at 0.4 m/s.

DNF at 26% with 9 touches: trailer rear-left hit the left rail near 23 m, and the front-right corner hit the right rail on every pull-forward retry. Do not retry the same spot: each short pull-forward and re-reverse hit the same place, and steering right while pulling forward hit the right rail. Before about 18 m, stop and study the rails with the left mirror and camera. Swing the trailer rear well right of the left pinch early, pull forward straight and far, reverse at about 1 m/s, and ration the 8 touches.

DNF with 9 touches, 7 on the trailer rear-left corner near 23-25 m of reversing, where the left rail pinches in; 2 more on the vehicle front-right while pulling forward steered right. A late rightward hitch bias at slow speed did not clear it. Likely the whole rig is too far left before that spot, so fix the path in the first 15 m instead. Mirror guards triggered too late. Do not retry the same spot; ration touches.
